kannappa.riddle: A hunter offered his god meat, river water carried in his mouth, and then his own eyes.
kannappa.story: Thinnan was a hunter who worshipped Shiva at Srikalahasti in his own rough way. To test him, Shiva made the lingam's eye bleed. Thinnan cut out his own eye with an arrow and pressed it into place. When the second eye began to bleed, he set his foot on the lingam to mark the spot, so he could find it after blinding himself. Shiva stopped him. He became Kannappa, one of the 63 Nayanmar saints.
kannappa.lookCloser: His foot is on the lingam, marking the spot.

govardhana.riddle: A boy held up a mountain for seven days so nobody got wet.
govardhana.story: Krishna persuaded the people of Vraja to honour Govardhana hill instead of Indra. Indra answered with seven days of storms. Krishna lifted the whole hill and held it up as an umbrella for the people and their cattle, until Indra gave up.
govardhana.lookCloser: The cows resting safely under the hill.

manthan.riddle: Gods and demons in a tug-of-war, with a snake for a rope and a mountain for a stick.
manthan.story: The devas and asuras churned the ocean of milk to win amrita, the nectar of immortality. Mount Mandara was the churning rod and the serpent Vasuki was the rope. When the mountain began to sink, Vishnu became Kurma, a tortoise, and held it up on his back. The first thing to rise was a deadly poison, halahala, which Shiva drank to save the world.
manthan.lookCloser: Kurma's head peeking out under the mountain. Which team is holding the snake's head end?

kaliya.riddle: A child danced on a many-headed problem.
kaliya.story: The serpent Kaliya had poisoned the Yamuna so badly that birds fell from the sky above it. The young Krishna dived in and danced on Kaliya's hoods until the serpent gave in. He spared Kaliya's life and sent him away from the river.
kaliya.lookCloser: Krishna is holding Kaliya's tail as he dances.

ranganatha.riddle: Asleep on a snake that floats on an ocean.
ranganatha.story: Vishnu rests on the serpent Adisesha, floating on the cosmic ocean between the cycles of creation. In this reclining form he is worshipped as Ranganatha at Srirangam.
ranganatha.lookCloser: The five hoods sheltering his head.

durga.riddle: The reason these nine nights exist, riding a lion.
durga.story: The buffalo demon Mahishasura had a boon that no man or god could kill him. The gods combined their powers into Durga. She fought him for nine nights and killed him on the tenth day, Vijayadashami.
durga.lookCloser: Her trident striking the demon as he emerges from the buffalo.

murugan.riddle: A general whose enemy became his ride.
murugan.story: Murugan, son of Shiva and Parvati, led the gods' army against the asura Surapadman. He split Surapadman in two with his vel, a spear his mother gave him. The two halves became his peacock mount and the rooster on his banner.

sanjeevani.riddle: He couldn't find the right herb, so he brought the whole mountain.
sanjeevani.story: In the war at Lanka, Lakshmana was struck down. Only the sanjeevani herb, which grew on a Himalayan peak, could save him before dawn. Hanuman flew there but couldn't tell which plant it was, so he lifted the whole peak and carried it back.
sanjeevani.lookCloser: The mountain balanced on his palm.
